title: SNMP Information Disclosure (Default / Public Community String)

references.name: MITRE ATT&CK - T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery

description: Network devices expose SNMP using default or guessable community strings (such as "public" or "private") over SNMP v1/v2c, which transmit data without encryption. An attacker can read device configuration, routing tables, interfaces, ARP/CAM tables, and sometimes credentials; writable strings may permit configuration changes.
businessImpact: Moderate --- disclosed network and device detail aids mapping and targeting; a writable community string can allow device reconfiguration and disruption.
remediation:
- Disable SNMP where unused; otherwise migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption.
- Replace default community strings with strong, unique values and make strings read-only where possible.
- Restrict SNMP access to dedicated management hosts and networks via ACLs.
- Monitor for unauthorized SNMP queries.
